title: Fish and taters
html_source:
Bloom here remembers that 17 JUN 1904 falls on a Friday, during which practising Catholics (at the time) were to abstain from meat. It is unlikely that he would be able to purchase anything to eat on a Friday in Catholic Dublin other than seafood and vegetables. He chooses in the next paragraph to purchase meat (at the last possible moment) for later consumption, thereby demonstrating his relaxed attitude toward Friday abstinence.

The Irish for “Friday” is “Aoine,” which translates literally as “fasting.”
